correctness.rationale: Write B=p/q and C=r/s reduced with polynomial numerator degrees d and e and denominator analytic/nonvanishing on closed disk. Their nonzero elimination resultant Res_z(p-uq,r-vs) has bidegree <=(e,d) and vanishes identically after (u,v)=(B(z),C(z)). Thus the (e+1)(d+1) unit H^2 vectors B^j C^k are linearly dependent. For comparable distinct index pairs, zero values at origin make the off-diagonal Gram inner products vanish. Only opposite-sign differences can contribute a mixed moment in the prescribed rectangle, with at most j(d-k)+(e-j)k<=de entries per row. If each were <1/(de) all unit-diagonal Gram rows would be strictly diagonally dominant and hence nonsingular, contradicting the resultant dependence. Coprime monomial B=z^d,C=z^e has first nonzero mixed moment exactly at (m,n)=(e,d), proving separate exponent-cutoff necessity; degree one attains bound. Independently evaluated all 625 (d,e) combinations through 25 for maximum row count and coprime monomial examples. The analytic resultant/Gershgorin proof, not these tests, proves arbitrary degrees.
